properties.name: An objection counts against a claim as far as the objection itself holds: it refutes when it holds, contests while unknown, and stops counting once answered
properties.rationale: Anthony chose "Contest until established" on 2026-10-16, at the start of requirement A (req:a-design-holds-a-line-of-reasoning). Requirement A needs an argument for and against to keep both sides with no verdict. B's rule (merged in #760, never released) made ANY opposing CONTRADICTS fail its target, so recording an objection delivered a verdict by structure alone, and a counterexample later shown wrong still sank the claim. Weighing the objection by its own truth matches how support already works: a conclusion holds only when its premises do. It is also how argumentation reads an attack: an argument is defeated only by an attacker that stands. Not chosen: keep B's rule and mark contesting objections with a new value on the link.
